text:
Berkly Catton has a point in eight straight games and 14 in 16 overall, and Sound Of Hockey wonders if he is the star Seattle has waited for. At 20, the eighth pick of 2024 has jumped from 0.26 points a game as a rookie to 0.88, with his ice time up two minutes to about 15 a night and a bigger power-play role.

The role change is the durable part, and our numbers flag it as a breakout. His line has also been Seattle's best: Alison Lukan wrote that Catton's line led the way in the win over Calgary, and with him on the ice the Kraken have 56% of expected goals, 14 points better than without him.

The scoring pace needs a discount. He has five goals on 2.71 expected and is shooting 20%, and his points per 60 sit far above his range. Among forwards drafted sixth to tenth since 2005, the median first full season is 0.41 points a game, a better guide than a hot month. His transition game (52% of his shots off the rush last season, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) is why the role looks earned.
headline: Berkly Catton's point streak is a breakout in progress
